result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.compose()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compose this graph with another graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12703-L12756){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.compose(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Similar to union, but the other graph's node attributes/labels take precedence over this graph's. Useful when you want to merge updates from another graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph to compose with (its attributes take precedence). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new composed graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graphs have different directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - Similar to union but other graph's attributes take precedence - Useful for applying updates to a base graph ## Examples {.doc-examples} Merge with attribute updates: ::: {#1d5e1e68 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Original graph g1 = ec.Graph(directed=False) g1.add_node(label="Alice") g1.add_node(label="Bob") g1.add_edge("Alice", "Bob") # Updates (new label for node 2) g2 = ec.Graph(directed=False) g2.add_node(label="Robert") # Node 1 with new label # Compose: g2's labels override g1's result = g1.compose(g2) # Node 1 now has label "Robert" instead of "Alice" ``` :::
